vocab.definition: a particle 1–100 nm across (a few hundred atoms).
ratio that increases as particles get smaller.
the study of very small structures and their uses.

misconceptions.wrong: Smaller particles have a smaller surface area : volume ratio.
misconceptions.right: Smaller particles have a much LARGER ratio.

misconceptions.wrong: Nanoparticles behave the same as bulk material.
misconceptions.right: They can have very different properties.
Their effects on health are not yet fully known.

infoPanels.title: SURFACE AREA : VOLUME
workedSteps: A cube of side 2: SA = 6×(2²) = 24, V = 2³ = 8.
A cube of side 1: SA = 6, V = 1.
Smaller cube → bigger surface area : volume ratio.

questions.text: State the size range of a nanoparticle. [1 mark]
A cube has side 3 nm. Calculate its surface area : volume ratio. [2 marks]
Explain why a high surface area : volume ratio makes nanoparticles good catalysts. [2 marks]
Give one use of nanoparticles (e.g. in sun cream or medicine). [1 mark]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: As particles get ______, the surface area : volume ratio gets ______.

questions.text: Suggest why some people are concerned about using nanoparticles. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Halving the size roughly doubles the surface area : volume ratio.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does a larger surface area mean less material can be used?
